description:
I am, MUGISHA ALVIN a technology enthusiast and aspiring web developer passionate about innovation, science and space exploration.

S-Crew is participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge with our project, Abandoned but not Forgotten, an interactive website exploring NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

We welcome passionate participants skilled in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, UI/UX design, graphic design, astronomy, research and storytelling.
summary:
Space Crew developed an interactive web platform designed to tell the hidden stories of NASA’s discarded equipment across the Moon and Mars.
Through engaging digital storytelling, interactive mission timelines, and detailed artifact profiles, our website transforms complex NASA planetary archives into an accessible, visually captivating experience. Users can explore the exact locations, technical purposes, and historical journeys of left-behind rovers, landers, and scientific instruments—from the Apollo lunar modules to retired Martian explorers.
This directly addresses the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by bridging the gap between raw aerospace data and public imagination, ensuring these pioneering machines are remembered for their contributions rather than forgotten as space debris.
Preserving the legacy of these artifacts is vital for inspiring future generations of space explorers, fostering public appreciation for scientific milestones, and highlighting the evolving environmental and historical stewardship of off-world exploration.
details:
Team Space Crew from Kampala, Uganda developed Beyond the Mission, a lightweight, interactive storytelling website that brings the history of NASA’s discarded space hardware to life.

​Since 1961, NASA has left over 200 tons of equipment across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Our platform directly addresses the challenge by transforming dense archival data from NASA’s PDS, NSSDCA, and JPL into accessible, human-centered stories centered around three iconic heroes: the Apollo 17 Lunar Rover, Mars rover Opportunity ("Oppy"), and Voyager 1. Built with open web standards (HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript) for low-bandwidth and mobile accessibility, the site brings planetary exploration directly into local classrooms.

​Preserving these narratives is vital because it reframes retired spacecraft from "space junk" into silent monuments of human bravery and ingenuity. By connecting NASA’s 60-year legacy with Uganda’s own emergence as a space-faring nation following the launch of PearlAfricaSat-1 (Abandoned-1), our project inspires young students across Uganda and the world to become the next generation of builders creating technology worth remembering.
